paper.title: Copeland Dueling Bandit Problem: Regret Lower Bound, Optimal Algorithm, and Computationally Efficient Algorithm

unmapped: mu_ij != 1/2 for all i != j (no ties in the preference matrix)
regret per round r_ij = (L_i + L_j - 2 L_1)/(2(K-1)) based on Copeland numbers
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t=1,2,\dots,T$, the forecaster draws a pair of arms $p(t) = (l(t), m(t)) \in [K]^2$ and, receives relative feedback $\myX{l(t)}{m(t)}(t) \sim \Bernoulli(\muij{l(t)}{m(t)})$ ... We define the regret per round is $\reg{i}{j} := (\Li{i} + \Li{j} - 2 \Li{1}) / (2(K-1)) \le 1$ when the pair $(i,j)$ is compared and the regret as $ \Regret(T) := \sum_{t \in [T]} \reg{l(t)}{m(t)}$.

settings.name_in_paper: K-armed Copeland dueling bandit problem (lower bound)
unmapped: mu_ij != 1/2 for all i != j (no ties in the preference matrix)
regret per round r_ij = (L_i + L_j - 2 L_1)/(2(K-1)) based on Copeland numbers
settings.definition_quote: A Copeland dueling bandit algorithm is strongly consistent if it satisfies $\Expect[\Regret(T)] = \so(T^a)$ for any $a>0$ given any preference matrix $\Mat \in \mcop$.

algorithms.name: CW-RMED (Copeland Winners Relative Minimum Empirical Divergence)

symbols.C_star: min over Copeland winners i_1 of C*_{i_1}({mu_ij}), the value of the LP minimizing regret-weighted exploration subject to the identification constraints R_{i_1}

source.label: thm_regretlower
source.quote: The regret of a strongly consistent algorithm is lower bounded as: \Expect[\Regret(T)]\ge \min_{i_1 \in \winners} \optcone{i_1}(\{\muij{i}{j}\}) \log{T}-\so(\log T).

results.notes: Strongly consistent = E[R(T)] = o(T^a) for all a>0 on all preference matrices. Regret is defined through Copeland numbers of drawn pairs, mapped to pseudo_regret. Derived from Lemma 1 (lower bound on weighted draw counts), not recorded separately.

symbols.C_star: min over Copeland winners i_1 of C*_{i_1}({mu_ij}), the LP value from the lower bound

conditions: the optimal solution set R*_{i_1}({mu_ij}) is unique for each Copeland winner i_1

source.label: thm_opt
source.quote: Assume that $\argmin_{i_1 \in \winners} \optcone{i_1}(\{\muij{i}{j}\})$ and $\optset{i_1}{\{\muij{i}{j}\}}$ for each $i_1 \in \winners$ are unique. For any $\algalpha > 0$, $\algbeta>0$, the regret of CW-RMED is bounded as: \Expect[\Regret(T)]\le \min_{i_1 \in \winners} \optcone{i_1}(\{\muij{i}{j}\}) \log T +\so(\log T).

results.notes: Matches Theorem 2 lower bound (asymptotically optimal). Computation: paper says the LP has exponentially many constraints, solvable in polynomial time via ellipsoid with separation oracle, but abstract says efficiency is not known; recorded as not_stated. Algorithm uses only log t, so treated as anytime.

symbols.C_E: min over Copeland winners i_1 of C^{E*}_{i_1}({mu_ij}), the value of the relaxed (more restrictive) LP used by ECW-RMED; C_E >= C_star with equality when there are >= 2 Copeland winners (Theorem 6)

conditions: the optimal solution set R^{E*}_{i_1}({mu_ij}) is unique for each Copeland winner i_1

source.label: thm_relax
source.quote: Assume that $\argmin_{i_1 \in \winners} \optconerelax{i}(\{\muij{i}{j}\})$ and $\optsetrelax{i_1}{\{\muij{i}{j}\}}$ for each $i_1 \in \winners$ are unique. For any $\algalpha > 0$, $\algbeta>0$, the regret of ECW-RMED is bounded as: \Expect[\Regret(T)]\le \min_{i_1 \in \winners} \optconerelax{i_1}(\{\muij{i}{j}\}) \log T +\so(\log T).

results.notes: Theorem 6 shows C_E >= C_star always and C_E = C_star when C >= 2 (so ECW-RMED is optimal with multiple Copeland winners). Text further gives C_E <= (1/kl(1/2+Delta,1/2)) sum_{i2} (1 + L_{i2}/(L_{i2}-L_1+1)) <= K/kl(1/2+Delta,1/2)*((L_1+3)/2 + L_1^2/K) (informal derivations, not recorded). Theorem 5 gives efficient sorting-based LP solution.

cited_results.setting_description: Stochastic K-armed Copeland dueling bandit; C = number of Copeland winners, L_1 = number of arms beating a Copeland winner, Delta = min_{i>j} |mu_ij - 1/2| (looser than original)
